newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govmt wants to replace Paris police chief.
newsitem.headline: French govmt wants to replace Paris police chief.

text.p: France's new left-wing government is demanding the replacement of a Paris police chief suspended for refusing to help a sleaze probe into conservative Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, official sources said on Thursday.
The government sent President Jacques Chirac, a close ally of Tiberi, a decree transferring Olivier Foll, head of the Paris criminal police, to a less sensitive post, they said.

The decree needs to be signed by Chirac, who was Paris mayor until 1995 when his deputy Tiberi took over, and will provide a test of the "cohabitation" between the conservative president and the Socialist-led government.
The previous, conservative government had kept Foll in his job in an open challenge to courts which had suspended his investigative capacities.
The sources said Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement, who took office last week, wanted Foll, 58, to be replaced by Patrick Riou, 50, currently spokesman of the national police headquarters.

The supreme court in February upheld a six-month suspension of Foll's investigative capacities after he ordered his men last June to refuse to help an investigating magistrate search Tiberi's home last year.
Magistrate Eric Halphen was looking for evidence in a far-reaching investigation into alleged illicit funding of Chirac's Gaullist RPR party through rake-offs on public housing contracts.
Ex-interior minister Jean-Louis Debre, also a senior member of the RPR, had publicly backed Foll and kept him at his post.
The left-leaning Magistrates' Union wrote to Chevenement earlier this week, saying that it was "intolerable" that Foll had stayed on. It also called for less political control on the judicial police.
